parts.name: Capsule
parts.description: Capsule: dense irregular connective tissue (type I collagen) enclosing the node and thickened at the hilum. Afferent lymphatics pierce it on the convex surface; trabeculae run inwards from it.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Capsule
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Capsule: dense irregular connective tissue (type I collagen) enclosing the node and thickened at the hilum. Afferent lymphatics pierce it on the convex surface; trabeculae run inwards from it.

parts.name: Trabeculae
parts.description: Trabeculae: connective-tissue septa that run from the capsule towards the hilum, partly dividing the cortex into compartments and carrying blood vessels; in the medulla they become the medullary trabeculae converging on the hilum.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Trabeculae
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Trabeculae: connective-tissue septa that run from the capsule towards the hilum, partly dividing the cortex into compartments and carrying blood vessels; in the medulla they become the medullary trabeculae converging on the hilum.

parts.name: Hilum connective tissue
parts.description: Hilum: the indentation on the concave side where the artery enters and the vein and efferent lymphatic leave, packed with connective tissue and fat continuous with the capsule.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Hilum connective tissue
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Hilum: the indentation on the concave side where the artery enters and the vein and efferent lymphatic leave, packed with connective tissue and fat continuous with the capsule.

parts.name: Subcapsular sinus
parts.description: Subcapsular (marginal) sinus: the space under the capsule into which afferent lymph pours. It is crossed by reticular fibres and lined by endothelium; its macrophages and the floor's subcapsular-sinus macrophages capture particles and hand antigen to the follicles beneath. Metastatic carcinoma cells lodge here first, so a sentinel node is examined under the capsule.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Subcapsular sinus
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. parts.name: Trabecular sinuses
parts.description: Trabecular (cortical) sinuses: channels alongside the trabeculae that carry lymph from the subcapsular sinus through the cortex to the medullary sinuses.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Trabecular sinuses
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Trabecular (cortical) sinuses: channels alongside the trabeculae that carry lymph from the subcapsular sinus through the cortex to the medullary sinuses.

parts.name: Outer cortex (B-cell zone)
parts.description: Outer (superficial) cortex: the B-cell zone. Between the follicles lies diffuse lymphoid tissue on a meshwork of reticular cells and fibres.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Outer cortex (B-cell zone)
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Outer (superficial) cortex: the B-cell zone. Between the follicles lies diffuse lymphoid tissue on a meshwork of reticular cells and fibres.

parts.name: Primary follicles
parts.description: Primary follicles: round, uniformly dense clusters of naive (IgM+ IgD+) B cells on a meshwork of follicular dendritic cells, seen before antigen stimulation. They have no germinal centre.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Primary follicles
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Primary follicles: round, uniformly dense clusters of naive (IgM+ IgD+) B cells on a meshwork of follicular dendritic cells, seen before antigen stimulation. They have no germinal centre.

parts.name: Mantle zone (secondary follicles)
parts.description: Mantle zone (corona): the dark rim of small, resting naive B cells pushed aside by the expanding germinal centre; it is thickest on the capsular side, forming a 'cap'. Mantle cell lymphoma (cyclin D1, t(11;14)) arises here.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Mantle zone (secondary follicles)
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Mantle zone (corona): the dark rim of small, resting naive B cells pushed aside by the expanding germinal centre; it is thickest on the capsular side, forming a 'cap'. Mantle cell lymphoma (cyclin D1, t(11;14)) arises here.

parts.name: Germinal centre - light zone
parts.description: Germinal centre - light zone (capsular pole): centrocytes, follicular dendritic cells holding antigen-antibody complexes and follicular helper T cells. Centrocytes compete for antigen and T-cell help: those with high-affinity receptors survive (affinity maturation), switch class and leave as plasma cells or memory B cells; the rest die by apoptosis and are eaten by tingible-body macrophages. Follicular lymphoma (BCL2, t(14;18)) mimics these follicles but lacks polarity and tingible-body macrophages.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Germinal centre - light zone
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Germinal centre - light zone (capsular pole): centrocytes, follicular dendritic cells holding antigen-antibody complexes and follicular helper T cells. Centrocytes compete for antigen and T-cell help: those with high-affinity receptors survive (affinity maturation), switch class and leave as plasma cells or memory B cells; the rest die by apoptosis and are eaten by tingible-body macrophages. Follicular lymphoma (BCL2, t(14;18)) mimics these follicles but lacks polarity and tingible-body macrophages.

parts.name: Germinal centre - dark zone
parts.description: Germinal centre - dark zone (medullary pole): densely packed, rapidly dividing centroblasts that undergo somatic hypermutation of their immunoglobulin genes (AID enzyme). A germinal centre marks a secondary follicle - one responding to antigen, 1-3 weeks after exposure.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Germinal centre - dark zone
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Germinal centre - dark zone (medullary pole): densely packed, rapidly dividing centroblasts that undergo somatic hypermutation of their immunoglobulin genes (AID enzyme). A germinal centre marks a secondary follicle - one responding to antigen, 1-3 weeks after exposure.

parts.name: Paracortex (T-cell zone)
parts.description: Paracortex (deep cortex): the thymus-dependent T-cell zone between the follicles and the medulla. Dendritic cells arriving in afferent lymph present antigen to T cells here. It expands in viral infections and is depleted in DiGeorge syndrome and after thymectomy in infancy.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Paracortex (T-cell zone)
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Paracortex (deep cortex): the thymus-dependent T-cell zone between the follicles and the medulla. Dendritic cells arriving in afferent lymph present antigen to T cells here. It expands in viral infections and is depleted in DiGeorge syndrome and after thymectomy in infancy.

parts.name: High endothelial venules
parts.description: High endothelial venules: postcapillary venules of the paracortex lined by plump cuboidal endothelium. Naive T and B cells leave the blood here - L-selectin binds peripheral node addressin, CCL19/CCL21 activate integrins - so about 90 % of the lymphocytes entering a node arrive from the blood, not the lymph.

parts.name: Anterior cover: High endothelial venules
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. High endothelial venules: postcapillary venules of the paracortex lined by plump cuboidal endothelium. Naive T and B cells leave the blood here - L-selectin binds peripheral node addressin, CCL19/CCL21 activate integrins - so about 90 % of the lymphocytes entering a node arrive from the blood, not the lymph.

parts.name: Medullary cords
parts.description: Medullary cords: branching cords of lymphoid tissue rich in plasma cells, macrophages and lymphocytes, continuous with the paracortex. Plasma cells secrete antibody straight into the efferent lymph.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Medullary cords
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Medullary cords: branching cords of lymphoid tissue rich in plasma cells, macrophages and lymphocytes, continuous with the paracortex. Plasma cells secrete antibody straight into the efferent lymph.

parts.name: Medullary sinuses
parts.description: Medullary sinuses: wide, tortuous lymph channels between the medullary cords, lined by discontinuous endothelium and full of macrophages; they converge on the efferent lymphatic at the hilum.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Medullary sinuses
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Medullary sinuses: wide, tortuous lymph channels between the medullary cords, lined by discontinuous endothelium and full of macrophages; they converge on the efferent lymphatic at the hilum.

parts.name: Reticular fibre meshwork
parts.description: Reticular fibre meshwork (type III collagen) spun by fibroblastic reticular cells across the sinuses and through the whole node. It slows the lymph so macrophages can filter it, and in the cortex its fibres are sheathed as conduits that deliver small soluble antigens to the high endothelial venules and dendritic cells. Shown by silver stains.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Reticular fibre meshwork
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Reticular fibre meshwork (type III collagen) spun by fibroblastic reticular cells across the sinuses and through the whole node. It slows the lymph so macrophages can filter it, and in the cortex its fibres are sheathed as conduits that deliver small soluble antigens to the high endothelial venules and dendritic cells. Shown by silver stains.

parts.name: Sinus macrophages
parts.description: Sinus macrophages: phagocytes clinging to the reticular meshwork of the sinuses. They remove bacteria, debris and particles - carbon pigment (anthracosis) in thoracic nodes, tattoo ink in axillary nodes - and present antigen.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Sinus macrophages
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Sinus macrophages: phagocytes clinging to the reticular meshwork of the sinuses. They remove bacteria, debris and particles - carbon pigment (anthracosis) in thoracic nodes, tattoo ink in axillary nodes - and present antigen.

parts.name: Afferent lymphatic vessels
parts.description: Afferent lymphatic vessels: several thin-walled collecting lymphatics that pierce the capsule on the convex surface and empty into the subcapsular sinus. Their valves force one-way flow into the node, and the swelling just beyond each valve gives the vessel its beaded look.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Afferent lymphatic vessels
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Afferent lymphatic vessels: several thin-walled collecting lymphatics that pierce the capsule on the convex surface and empty into the subcapsular sinus. Their valves force one-way flow into the node, and the swelling just beyond each valve gives the vessel its beaded look.

parts.name: Efferent lymphatic vessel
parts.description: Efferent lymphatic vessel: leaves at the hilum carrying filtered lymph, plasma-cell antibody and activated lymphocytes onward to the next node in the chain and ultimately to the thoracic or right lymphatic duct. There is usually only one, and it has valves.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Efferent lymphatic vessel
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Efferent lymphatic vessel: leaves at the hilum carrying filtered lymph, plasma-cell antibody and activated lymphocytes onward to the next node in the chain and ultimately to the thoracic or right lymphatic duct. There is usually only one, and it has valves.

parts.name: Lymphatic valves
parts.description: Lymphatic valves: paired semilunar cusps of endothelium on a thin connective-tissue core whose free edges point downstream - towards the node in afferent vessels, away from it in the efferent vessel.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Lymphatic valves
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Lymphatic valves: paired semilunar cusps of endothelium on a thin connective-tissue core whose free edges point downstream - towards the node in afferent vessels, away from it in the efferent vessel.

parts.name: Artery (hilar and medullary branches)
parts.description: Nodal artery: enters at the hilum, runs in the medullary cords and trabeculae and breaks into a capillary bed in the cortex whose postcapillary venules are the high endothelial venules.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Artery (hilar and medullary branches)
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Nodal artery: enters at the hilum, runs in the medullary cords and trabeculae and breaks into a capillary bed in the cortex whose postcapillary venules are the high endothelial venules.

parts.name: Vein (hilar and medullary tributaries)
parts.description: Nodal vein: formed from the high endothelial venules and medullary veins, leaves at the hilum beside the artery.

parts.name: Anterior cover: Vein (hilar and medullary tributaries)
parts.description: Reversible positive-z section cover. Restore with the posterior part for complete source anatomy. Nodal vein: formed from the high endothelial venules and medullary veins, leaves at the hilum beside the artery.
